findings.claim: The new two-branch cause in the fill-the-checklist control is right for the likely cases but has two small wording gaps. (1) For a floated or absolutely positioned tag the browser blockifies the computed display, so the message reads 'the tag itself is not an ordinary block (its display is block, or it is floated or absolutely positioned)'. Probes on a private copy of the completed work confirmed this text for both cases. Saying 'not an ordinary block' and then 'its display is block' in the same clause is self-contradictory. The words that follow ('or it is floated or absolutely positioned' and 'remove that display, float or position change') still point the learner to the right fix. (2) A tag given display: contents has no box, and the ownLayout test does not cover that display value, so the message blames 'something around the tag (a wrapper, a float beside it, columns or positioning on the checklist)'. README Troubleshooting line 208 says 'the message names the cause', which is not true for this case. I grade this low, not as the rubric's high 'false claim', for two reasons. display: contents is an implausible edit for a padded, bordered tag, because the padding and border then stop drawing. And the float and absolute cases already name the right fix. The inline-block, inline-flex and table probes print their real display value and the right cause.
findings.recommendation: When the tag is floated or absolutely positioned, name that instead of printing the computed display: for example, say 'it is floated' or 'it is absolutely positioned', and print the display value only for inline-* or table-* displays. Treat display: contents (a tag with no box) as a tag-side cause too. Alternatively, soften the README Troubleshooting sentence to 'the message names the likely cause'.

items.note: At a942501c the control computes ownLayout from the tag's own computed display (inline*, table*), float and absolute or fixed position, and gives one of two causes. Probes on a private copy of the completed work: tags given inline-block, inline-flex or table display print that display and say the tag itself is not an ordinary block and shrinks to its text, with the fix 'remove that display, float or position change'. Floated tags and absolutely positioned tags get the same tag-side cause; their printed display wording is a polish gap, raised as low cl4-edu-001. A plain fixed-width wrapper, a padded wrapper and a multicolumn checklist with automatic-width tags each get the 'something around the tag' cause. Each case fails only task 11. README Troubleshooting line 208 now names both causes with inline-block, table, float and absolute examples. Together with the Outcome line 'Both stay ordinary blocks directly in the gear checklist', a learner can now tell what an ordinary block excludes. The narrowing remains fair for o2: it keeps the 200px on the tag's own width. Block-level flex, list-item, an unstyled wrapper and relative offsets all pass. That is harmless leniency, since the stated requirement is stricter than the test. The solved-run variantRuns sentence now attributes inline-block, table and float to the tag's own display or float, which matches my probes.
